name: Piru
body:
PIRU
CR 11

This hazy creature wears classic features associated with demons.

XP 12,800
CE Small outsider (chaotic, demon, evil, extraplanar, incorporeal)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +23

DEFENSE

AC 21, touch 21, flat-footed 16 (+5 deflection, +4 Dex, +1 dodge, +1 size)
hp 133 (14d10+56)
Fort +10, Ref +13, Will +11
Defensive Abilities incorporeal; Immune electricity, poison; Resist acid 10, cold 10, fire 10

OFFENSE

Speed fly 40 ft. (perfect)
Melee 2 touches +19 (4d8 negative energy)
Special Attacks battle of wits, telekinesis

STATISTICS

Str —, Dex 19, Con 19, Int 16, Wis 14, Cha 21
Base Atk +14; CMB +17; CMD 33
Feats Alertness, Dodge, Flyby Attack, Great Fortitude, Mobility, Skill Focus (Knowledge [nature], Knowledge [planes])
Skills Bluff +22, Fly +24, Intimidate +22, Knowledge (nature, planes) +26, Perception +23, Perform (oratory) +22, Sense Motive +23, Spellcraft +20, Stealth +18
Languages Abyssal, Celestial, Common; telepathy 100 ft.

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Battle of Wits (Su)

A piru can promise an opponent a great reward for winning a battle of wits. At the GMs discretion, this can be a riddle or an opposed Knowledge (nature or planes) check.

If the creature fails, it takes 2d4 points of drain for an ability of the piru’s choosing other than Intelligence, and the piru gains DR 10/— and SR 22 with respect to the creature’s attacks, spells, and abilities. A creature with an ability score reduced to 0 dies instantly. If the creature succeeds, the piru disappears and leaves a treasure appropriate to its CR and usable by the creature. While the piru questions the creature, it can attempt a Bluff check opposed by the creature’s Sense Motive. If the piru succeeds, the creature takes a ?4 penalty on any checks related to the current use of battle of wits. If the creature succeeds, it sees through the deceit and gains a +2 circumstance bonus on all checks related to any use of this piru’s battle of wits for 1 hour, and the piru can’t attempt another Bluff check against the creature for the duration.

Telekinesis (Su)

A piru augments its melee attacks with telekinesis.

This ability functions as the spell telekinesis, usable at will, with a caster level equal to the piru’s Hit Dice (CL 14 for most pirus). A typical piru has a ranged attack roll of +19 when using telekinesis to hurl objects or creatures and can use the ability on objects weighing up to 350 pounds. If a piru attempts to hurl a creature with this ability, that creature can resist the effect with a successful DC 22 Will save. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any forest (Abyss)
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Ghostly demons inhabiting the gnarled and tar-stained woods of the Abyss, pirus form out of the souls of those whose hubris resulted in their deaths. They regularly jaunt to the Material Plane in search of intelligent creatures that enjoy condescending to others based on their apparently superior intellect. Pirus propose battles of wits with these “smart alecks,” with the promise of incredible rewards for defeating the demons. Though they cagily avoid discussing the consequences of failure, they must disclose the price—the stealing of their opponents’ essence—if directly asked. Pirus refuse to reduce their foes’ intellect if they win and spread out the weakening effects among their foes’ attributes to toy with their targets and entice their targets to continue testing their wits. The demons collect the souls of creatures that die during these battles of wits, and these souls eventually form into new pirus.

When not engaged in their favorite sport, pirus use their telekinesis to frighten locals and sow chaos. They can harm their foes with a touch, but they much prefer to chuck inanimate objects or other creatures at their foes.

In areas with frequent enough piru activity, the local inhabitants use the name as an epithet for mischief-makers and those who bully others with their intellects.
